name: Lungomare and the Seafront
tagline: The rebuilt promenade along the bay, where the city gathers
description: Vlore's seafront was rebuilt in the last decade into a wide palm-lined promenade running the length of the bay, and it is now the centre of the city's social life, with cafes, restaurants and the evening walk that every Albanian town observes. Apartment blocks face it directly.
bestFor: Stays that want the promenade, the cafes and the sea directly outside
pros: The rebuilt promenade and the bay at the door
Cafes and restaurants along its whole length
The city's evening social life happens here
cons: The highest rents in Vlore, higher again in summer
Busy and loud through the season
New construction is ongoing along the front

name: City Centre and Flag Square
tagline: Around the independence monument and the old mosque
description: The commercial core inland from the seafront around Flag Square, where Albanian independence was declared in 1912, with the Muradie mosque, the market, the banks and the bus connections. It is the practical centre of the city and cheaper than anything facing the water.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market and services close and does not need a sea view
pros: Market, banks and all services within a short walk
Bus connections along the Riviera and to Tirana
cons: Mixed and sometimes poor building quality

name: Uji i Ftohte
tagline: The southern suburb where the coast road starts to climb
description: A residential and holiday district a few kilometres south where the bay narrows and the water is clearer, named for the cold springs that surface here. Newer apartment blocks, small hotels and a quieter beach, with the road onward towards the Llogara pass and the Riviera.
bestFor: Stays that want clearer water and less noise, still close to the city
pros: Cleaner water than the main city beach
On the road towards the Riviera and Llogara
cons: Ten minutes from the city centre
Heavy summer traffic on the coast road

name: Skele and the Port Side
tagline: The working harbour end, cheapest and most local
description: The northern part of the city around the ferry port for Brindisi and the older residential streets behind it, entirely local in character with markets, workshops and no tourism at all. Rents are the lowest in Vlore and the seafront is a fifteen-minute walk south.
bestFor: Long stays at the lowest cost, in a district with no tourist pricing
pros: The lowest rents in the city
Ferry to Italy from the doorstep
cons: Little to look at and no restaurants of note

name: Radhime and the Coast South (12 km)
tagline: The first stretch of the Riviera, below the Llogara climb
description: The coastal strip running south from Vlore towards the Llogara pass, where small hotels and apartments sit above pebble coves with the Karaburun peninsula opposite. The water is markedly clearer than in the bay and the road behind climbs into pine forest and mountain.
bestFor: Stays that want clear water and the Riviera rather than a city
pros: Clear water and quiet pebble coves
Karaburun peninsula and the marine park opposite
Llogara pass and its forest immediately behind
cons: Almost everything closes out of season
